body:
Stacked on #93 (base is its branch; retarget to `dev` when #93 merges). Draft.

## Why
Review of #93 found two real defects and one gap:
1. **A session was treated as proof of recovery** on `/auth/reset`: any signed-in user could change their password there. A paused agent's attempted fix read `amr` from the Session object (no such field) and accepted generic `otp`.
2. **Same-browser confirmation showed "Link expired" on a valid link.** The browser client exchanges `?code=` itself during init and consumes the verifier; the app's own second exchange then fails.
3. No test used a real email.

## What changed
- `/auth/reset` opens the form only when the **server accepts the token** (`getUser`) AND this tab recorded the recovery moment for this exact `session_id` (SDK `PASSWORD_RECOVERY` / our `verifyOtp(type=recovery)`; 1h; sessionStorage) OR the SDK-reported methods include a recent `recovery`. `otp`, `password`, `email/signup`, `magiclink` are never accepted. The recovery session is ended after the password changes.
- `confirmEmail` accepts a server-validated signup session created moments ago instead of re-exchanging; an older ordinary session is never mistaken for it.
- Carried (reviewed) from the paused agent's uncommitted work, provenance in commit 2: focus-once hook, `MmErrorPanel focusOnMount`, link-error tweaks, the Mailpit fixture and the e2e spec (reworked).
- **Not carried:** its reset-page rewrite, `isRecoveryContext`, `exchangeRecoveryCode` (races the SDK), and the `supabase/config.toml` edits (they would turn confirmations on and change redirect URLs for every local/CI stack).

## Measured (local GoTrue, auth-js 2.110.7)
| session source | amr | SDK event |
|---|---|---|
| password | `password` | SIGNED_IN |
| recovery, PKCE/implicit (GET /verify) | `recovery` | PASSWORD_RECOVERY |
| recovery, `verifyOtp` token_hash (POST /verify) | **`otp`** | PASSWORD_RECOVERY |
| signup confirmation | `email/signup` | SIGNED_IN |
| magic link | `magiclink` | SIGNED_IN |

## Evidence (LOCAL only; no hosted evidence yet)
- Unit: auth component tests 33/33 (each refused session type, server rejection, stale, reload, cross-session).
- Browser, isolated local stack + Mailpit, real emails, fresh contexts: **10/10 with token_hash templates** (cross-device confirm and recovery, reuse, cold, ordinary session, invalid, error focus, new-password login); earlier 8 pass + 2 skip with default PKCE templates.
- CI-style (no mail catcher): 3 mail-free tests pass, 7 skip by design.
- typecheck, lint clean.

## Not done
DEV email-template change and hosted verification are blocked (Supabase management token returned 401). Script ready, dry-run by default, saves a rollback copy: `apply-dev-auth-templates.cjs`.

commits.messageBody:
…omed second code exchange

Recovery proof
- A session is no proof of recovery. The reset form opens only when the server accepts the access token (getUser) AND
  either (a) this tab recorded the recovery moment for this exact session_id (the SDK emitted PASSWORD_RECOVERY / our
  verifyOtp(type=recovery) succeeded; sessionStorage marker, 1h window) or (b) the SDK-reported authentication methods
  include a recent `recovery` entry (links delivered by GET /verify). `otp`, `password`, `email/signup` and `magiclink`
  are never accepted. Measured on the local GoTrue: verifyOtp(recovery) is recorded as `otp`, PKCE/implicit recovery as
  `recovery`, signup as `email/signup`, magic link as `magiclink`.
- Replaces the paused agent's isRecoveryContext, which read `amr` from the Session object (it has no such field).
- The recovery session is ended after the password changes.

Confirmation
- The browser client exchanges `?code=` by itself while initialising and consumes the code verifier, so the app's own
  second exchange failed ("code verifier not found") on a valid same-browser link. confirmEmail now first accepts a
  server-validated signup session created moments ago, never an older ordinary session.

Tests: unit coverage for each refused session type, server rejection, stale sessions, marker reload and cross-session
refusal; e2e covers same-browser and cross-device (token_hash) confirmation and recovery, reuse, cold and ordinary-session
access against an isolated local stack with a real mail catcher.

session; its exchangeRecoveryCode races the SDK's own code exchange.
#93's link-errors, focus and config/template changes are kept.
